title_en: Special Provisions on the Labor Protection of Female Employees

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Provisions are formulated for the purpose of reducing and resolving the special difficulties caused by female workers' physiological characteristics during labor, and protecting female workers' health.

Article 2 These Provisions shall apply to state organs, enterprises, institutions, social organizations, individual economic organizations, and other social organizations as employers, as well as their female workers, within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 An employer shall strengthen the labor protection for female workers, take measures to improve the labor safety and health conditions for female workers, and provide training on labor safety and health knowledge to female workers.

Article 4 An employer shall comply with the provisions on the scope of labor prohibited for female workers. An employer shall inform in writing its female workers of the positions that fall within the scope of labor prohibited for female workers in the employer.
The scope of labor prohibited for female workers is specified in the appendix to these Provisions. The State Administration of Work Safety shall, jointly with the human resources and social security administrative department of the State Council and the health administrative department of the State Council, adjust the scope of labor prohibited for female workers based on the economic and social development conditions.
Article 5 An employer shall not reduce the wages of a female worker, dismiss her, or terminate the labor or employment contract with her because of her pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding.

Article 6 Where a female worker cannot adapt to her original work during pregnancy, the employer shall, based on the certificate from a medical institution, reduce her workload or arrange other work that she can adapt to.
For a female worker who has been pregnant for seven months or more, the employer shall not extend her working hours or arrange night shift work, and shall arrange a certain period of rest during working hours.
The time required for a pregnant female worker to undergo prenatal check-ups during working hours shall be counted as working hours.

Article 7 A female worker shall enjoy 98 days of maternity leave for childbirth, of which 15 days may be taken before childbirth; in case of dystocia, an additional 15 days of maternity leave shall be granted; in case of multiple births, an additional 15 days of maternity leave shall be granted for each additional baby born.
A female worker who has a miscarriage before four months of pregnancy shall enjoy 15 days of maternity leave; a female worker who has a miscarriage at four months of pregnancy or later shall enjoy 42 days of maternity leave.

Article 8 The maternity allowance during the maternity leave of a female worker shall, for those who have participated in maternity insurance, be paid by the maternity insurance fund according to the standard of the average monthly wage of the employees of the employer in the preceding year; for those who have not participated in maternity insurance, be paid by the employer according to the standard of the female worker's wage before the maternity leave.
The medical expenses incurred by a female worker due to childbirth or miscarriage shall, for those who have participated in maternity insurance, be paid by the maternity insurance fund according to the items and standards specified in the maternity insurance provisions; for those who have not participated in maternity insurance, be paid by the employer.

Article 9 For a female worker who is breastfeeding an infant under one year old, the employer shall not extend her working hours or arrange night shift work.
The employer shall arrange one hour of breastfeeding time for a breastfeeding female worker during each working day; where a female worker gives birth to multiple babies, an additional one hour of breastfeeding time per day shall be provided for each additional baby being breastfed.

Article 10 An employer with a relatively large number of female workers shall, based on the needs of female workers, establish facilities such as female workers' hygiene rooms, pregnant workers' rest rooms, and breastfeeding rooms, so as to properly address the difficulties of female workers in terms of physiological hygiene and breastfeeding.
Article 11 In the workplace, an employer shall prevent and stop sexual harassment against female workers.

Article 12 The human resources and social security administrative department and the work safety supervisory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for supervising and inspecting the compliance of employers with these Provisions.
Trade unions and women's organizations shall, according to law, supervise the compliance of employers with these Provisions.

Article 13 Where an employer violates Article 6, paragraph 2, Article 7, or Article 9, paragraph 1 of these Provisions, the human resources and social security administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a specified period, and impose a fine calculated at the standard of not less than RMB 1,000 nor more than RMB 5,000 per female worker harmed.
Where an employer violates Item 1 or Item 2 of the appendix to these Provisions, the work safety supervisory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a specified period, and impose a fine calculated at the standard of not less than RMB 1,000 nor more than RMB 5,000 per female worker harmed. Where an employer violates Item 3 or Item 4 of the appendix to these Provisions, the work safety supervisory department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order it to make corrections within a specified period, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 nor more than RMB 300,000; if the circumstances are serious, it shall order the suspension of relevant operations, or request the relevant people's government to order closure of the employer in accordance with the authority prescribed by the State Council.

Article 14 Where an employer violates these Provisions and infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a female worker, the female worker may, according to law, file a complaint, report, or petition, apply to a labor and personnel dispute mediation or arbitration institution for mediation or arbitration, and if dissatisfied with the arbitration award, may file a lawsuit with a People's Court according to law.

Article 15 Where an employer violates these Provisions, infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a female worker, and causes damage to the female worker, it shall provide compensation according to law; if the employer and its directly responsible person in charge and other directly liable persons constitute a crime, they shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.
